A method and an exhaust treatment system are provided for treatment of an exhaust stream comprising nitrogen oxides. The method comprises a first oxidation of compounds comprising one or more of nitrogen, carbon and hydrogen in the exhaust stream; a determination of a value for a ratio between a first amount of nitrogen dioxide and a first amount of nitrogen oxides after the first oxidation; and a first supply of a first additive into the exhaust stream, which is actively controlled based on the determined value for the ratio. outputs.L2: Disclosed are a process and an exhaust aftertreatment system for handling an exhaust flow containing nitrogen oxides. Initially, exhaust constituents that include at least one of nitrogen, carbon, or hydrogen are oxidized. Following this oxidation stage, the ratio of a first quantity of nitrogen dioxide to a first quantity of nitrogen oxides is calculated. A first additive is then introduced into the exhaust flow, with the amount supplied being actively regulated according to the calculated ratio. Thereafter, at least the first quantity of nitrogen oxides is reduced by a catalytic reaction within a catalytic filter. This filter consists of a particulate filter having a coating that is at least partially catalytic and possesses reduction properties. The filter is configured both to capture and oxidize soot particles and to reduce the first quantity of nitrogen oxides.
outputs.L3:
The method and exhaust treatment system are configured to treat an exhaust stream containing nitrogen oxides (NOₓ). In an initial oxidation stage, compounds containing nitrogen, carbon, and/or hydrogen are oxidized within the exhaust stream. After this oxidation stage, the ratio of nitrogen dioxide (NO₂) to the total amount of nitrogen oxides is determined.

Based on the determined NO₂-to-NOₓ ratio, a first additive is introduced into the exhaust stream. The quantity of the first additive is actively controlled to maintain or achieve suitable conditions for downstream emissions treatment. The treated exhaust stream is then directed through a catalytic particulate filter. The filter captures soot particles and promotes their oxidation while also catalytically reducing at least a first portion of the nitrogen oxides present in the exhaust stream.
outputs.L4:
The method is designed for treating exhaust gas that contains nitrogen oxides, particulate matter, and residual nitrogen-, carbon-, or hydrogen-containing compounds. In an initial oxidation step, at least some of these compounds are converted into more highly oxidized products. This step also adjusts the composition of the nitrogen oxides, particularly the relative concentrations of nitrogen monoxide and nitrogen dioxide. A sensor or measuring device determines the ratio of nitrogen dioxide to the total nitrogen-oxide content in the exhaust stream.

The measured ratio is supplied to a control unit, which uses it as a feedback variable for regulating the injection of an exhaust-treatment additive. The quantity, timing, or rate of additive injection is actively adjusted to maintain conditions favorable for nitrogen-oxide conversion while avoiding insufficient dosing or unnecessary additive consumption. The control system may respond continuously to changes in engine load, exhaust temperature, flow rate, and pollutant concentration, thereby maintaining effective treatment under varying operating conditions.

The conditioned exhaust gas subsequently passes through a particulate filter provided with a catalytic coating. The filter retains soot and other particulate matter, while the catalytic coating promotes reactions that reduce or otherwise convert nitrogen oxides into less harmful substances. Nitrogen dioxide present in the exhaust can also assist in oxidizing the accumulated soot, supporting passive or assisted regeneration of the filter and limiting excessive pressure buildup.

By combining ratio-based additive control with a catalytically active particulate filter, the method coordinates nitrogen-oxide reduction, particulate capture, and soot oxidation within a common exhaust-treatment stage. This integrated approach improves conversion efficiency, supports filter regeneration, and reduces the complexity and space requirements of the overall emissions-control system.

counterfactuals.output: A method and exhaust treatment system for treating exhaust gas from an internal combustion engine are disclosed. The exhaust gas is passed through an oxidation catalyst configured to oxidize one or more exhaust compounds, including conversion of at least a portion of nitric oxide (NO) to nitrogen dioxide (NO₂). A NO₂-to-NOx ratio downstream of the oxidation catalyst is determined using one or more sensors, an exhaust model, or a combination thereof. A controller regulates dosing of an additive into the exhaust gas based at least in part on the determined NO₂-to-NOx ratio. The dosed exhaust gas is then directed through a catalytically coated particulate filter configured to trap particulate matter and catalytically reduce NOx. Ratio-based dosing improves additive utilization and NOx conversion while limiting additive slip and supporting particulate-filter operation.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention for treating a diesel-engine exhaust stream containing nitrogen oxides, including active reductant dosing and a catalytic soot filter, using formal patent language.
counterfactuals.output:
**Title: Exhaust-Gas Treatment System Including Reductant Dosing and a Catalytically Active Particulate Filter**

An exhaust-gas treatment system is provided for treating an exhaust stream produced by a compression-ignition engine, the exhaust stream containing nitrogen oxides and particulate matter. The system comprises an exhaust conduit configured to receive the exhaust stream, a reductant delivery assembly operable to introduce a metered quantity of reductant or reductant precursor into the exhaust stream, and a catalytically active particulate filter positioned downstream of the reductant delivery assembly.

The reductant delivery assembly may comprise a reservoir, a dosing injector in fluid communication with the reservoir, and a controller configured to regulate injection as a function of one or more engine or exhaust-gas operating parameters. The reductant may comprise ammonia, an aqueous urea solution, a hydrocarbon, or another substance capable of providing a reducing species under exhaust conditions. A mixer or hydrolysis element may be disposed between the dosing injector and the particulate filter to promote evaporation, decomposition, and distribution of the reductant within the exhaust stream.

The particulate filter comprises a porous filter body configured to retain soot from the exhaust stream. At least a portion of the filter body carries a catalyst composition effective to promote selective reduction of nitrogen oxides in the presence of the dosed reductant. The catalyst composition may comprise a metal-exchanged molecular sieve, a vanadium-containing composition, a base-metal catalyst, or combinations thereof. The catalyst may be distributed substantially throughout the filter body or arranged in one or more longitudinal or radial zones.

During operation, the controller determines a desired reductant dosing rate based on signals representative of exhaust mass flow, exhaust temperature, engine load, nitrogen-oxide concentration, filter soot loading, or combinations thereof. Reductant is introduced upstream of the particulate filter and is conveyed into contact with the catalyst composition, whereby at least a portion of the nitrogen oxides is converted to nitrogen and water. Concurrently, particulate matter is captured within the porous filter body.

The controller may further implement a regeneration mode in which the temperature of the particulate filter is increased to oxidize accumulated soot. During regeneration, reductant dosing may be reduced, suspended, or otherwise adjusted to limit reductant slip and maintain catalyst durability. One or more nitrogen-oxide sensors, temperature sensors, pressure sensors, ammonia sensors, or differential-pressure sensors may be provided upstream or downstream of the particulate filter to enable closed-loop control of reductant delivery and filter regeneration.

Accordingly, the disclosed system provides combined particulate-matter filtration and nitrogen-oxide reduction within a compact exhaust-treatment architecture while permitting active control of reductant consumption, conversion efficiency, soot loading, and regeneration.

**Exemplary Independent Claim**

1. An exhaust-gas treatment apparatus for a diesel engine, comprising:  
   an exhaust passage configured to convey an exhaust stream containing nitrogen oxides and particulate matter;  
   a reductant dosing device configured to selectively introduce a reductant into the exhaust stream;  
   a particulate filter disposed downstream of the reductant dosing device and comprising a porous filter substrate carrying a catalyst effective to reduce nitrogen oxides in the presence of the reductant; and  
   a controller operatively coupled to the reductant dosing device and configured to control an amount of the reductant introduced into the exhaust stream based on at least one operating parameter of the diesel engine or the exhaust-gas treatment apparatus,  
   wherein the particulate filter is configured both to retain particulate matter and to catalyze conversion of at least a portion of the nitrogen oxides.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

A downstream sensor determines the NO₂/total-NOx ratio and supplies this value to a controller. counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a patent abstract for an integrated exhaust treatment system that simultaneously captures and oxidizes soot particles and catalytically reduces NOx after a controlled first oxidation and additive-supply step.
counterfactuals.output: An integrated exhaust treatment system includes a first oxidation stage configured to controllably oxidize one or more exhaust constituents, an additive-supply device positioned downstream of the first oxidation stage, a catalyzed particulate filter configured to capture and oxidize soot particles, and a selective catalytic reduction catalyst configured to reduce nitrogen oxides. A controller regulates the first oxidation stage and additive delivery based on sensed exhaust conditions to establish selected temperature, nitrogen dioxide concentration, and additive-to-NOx ratio. The particulate filter promotes continuous or intermittent soot oxidation while retaining particulate matter, and the reduction catalyst receives the conditioned, additive-containing exhaust to convert NOx to nitrogen. The coordinated arrangement enables simultaneous particulate capture and soot oxidation, controlled exhaust conditioning, and efficient downstream NOx reduction over a range of engine operating conditions.

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain, in one formal paragraph, a method for controlling urea or another additive in an exhaust system based on the measured NO₂:NOx ratio upstream of an SCR-coated particulate filter.
counterfactuals.output: A method for controlling an additive in an exhaust aftertreatment system comprises measuring concentrations of NO₂ and total NOx in exhaust gas upstream of a particulate filter having a selective catalytic reduction coating, calculating an upstream NO₂:NOx ratio, and supplying the calculated ratio, together with operating parameters such as exhaust temperature, mass flow, engine load, and filter state, to an electronic controller. The controller compares the measured ratio with a calibrated target ratio or operating map representing conditions for effective SCR conversion and particulate oxidation, determines a desired quantity of urea solution or another NOx-reducing additive, and commands an upstream dosing device accordingly. The commanded dose may be increased, reduced, delayed, or suspended to maintain a desired ammonia-to-NOx ratio while avoiding ammonia slip, deposit formation, catalyst saturation, or interference with filter regeneration, and the control action may be refined using downstream NOx or ammonia measurements in a closed-loop feedback arrangement.
